title: Chicken breast, fried, coated, skinless, coating edible, from raw

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken breast coated in a breadcrumb mixture and fried until golden. Cooking from raw preserves a high protein level, while the coating adds crunch and flavor. This product is common in quick meals, salads, and sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast is one of the leanest cuts, providing about 31 g of protein per 100 g.
Frying in a coating raises the calorie count but keeps the meat juicy.
Coatings can be made from wheat flour, breadcrumbs, spices, or dry dairy powders.
Traditionally served with sauces such as barbecue, honey‑mustard, or garlic aioli.
In some countries the dish is called “chicken breast cutlet.”

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Protein is essential for muscle growth, repair, and supporting the immune system.

items.title: Low fat in the meat itself
items.content: Skinless breast contains little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B3 (niacin) and B6 aid metabolism and support nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: phosphorus and selenium
items.content: Phosphorus is important for bones and teeth; selenium acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Satiety boost
items.content: The combination of protein and coating provides lasting fullness.

items.title: Increased calories from coating
items.content: Frying and breading add calories and fat, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Possible trans‑fat content
items.content: Certain breading mixes and oils can generate trans fats during high‑heat cooking.

items.title: Wheat or gluten allergy
items.content: The coating often contains wheat flour, which may be problematic for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Risk of excess sodium
items.content: Salt is commonly added to the coating; high sodium intake can raise blood pressure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried coated chicken breast can be served hot as a main dish, sliced into salads, used in sandwiches, or tossed with pasta. It pairs well with vegetable sides, mashed potatoes, or rice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked product in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 3 days. Freeze in an airtight container at –18 °C for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
